answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by weighting trust from diverse, independent endorsements, not raw identity count. An agent gains influence only when endorsed by counterparts who rarely interact — a comet visible from many shores, a jetty linking separate harbours, not a closed loop. Fake identities can endorse each other endlessly, but those endorsements cluster on one ridge of the trust graph and are discounted. Faking diversity forces an attacker to build real relationships and useful history in many independent communities, costing time, work, and reputation in each.
